rows.title: Device mission.start launches a ready write-scoped Mission with no device re-check
Mission-child reroute from ollama is bounded by constraints, so tool-capable reroute is blocked
rows.note: A tool-free mission child exists only when constraints.localOnly, budgetLocal or preferences.local is set (launchModel ~1229-1250 sets requiresFilesystem false only when localOnly). eligibility() then rejects every non-local provider (router.ts ~24-40: localOnly requires local_or_cloud==='local'). preLaunchRevalidate applies the same eligibility. codexMissionExclusion applies to missionAccess constraints. So the reroute candidates stay local, and no tool-capable local provider is routable (cline, opencode and cursor are detect-only).

rows.title: mission.retry from a device is refused at the HTTP and command layers
rows.note: DEVICE_RIGHTS has no mission.retry, so assertDeviceAction throws WORKSTATION_REQUIRED before dispatch (http.server.ts ~464; device-authority.server.ts DEVICE_RIGHTS). missionCommand REMOTE excludes mission.retry and refuses it for non-local access (commands.server.ts). Note: MissionManager.retry() (manager ~3447) has no actor guard of its own and relies on these layers.

rows.title: Replanned Mission cannot be started from a stale ready state
rows.note: mission.plan and mission.replan are not in DEVICE_RIGHTS (HTTP 400). replan() accepts only waiting_for_approval, waiting_for_user or failed, revokes the envelope, clears authorizationId, and plan() sets state waiting_for_approval (or failed). mission.start requires state==='ready'. Any child launch also runs taskViolation, which returns 'authorization revoked' for a revoked envelope (authorization.server.ts ~268).

rows.title: Device answers to provider.execute requests cannot launch tool-capable children
rows.note: deviceRequestRefusal (~1952-1960) returns APPROVAL_ON_HOST unless the child task is deviceMayLaunch (ollama, not a remote tag). respond() calls deviceRequestRefusal for non-deny decisions (~3200-3204). Write children cannot be ollama: requiresFilesystem is set for write steps and ollama's capabilities are text only. allow_batch on provider.execute creates a batch and reschedules the step (~3266 path). It never calls tasks.approve, and the relaunch creates a fresh child that runs taskViolation and agenticProviderCheck again. An allow_batch without a batchOffer is now a CommandRefusedError (~3220).

rows.title: Agentic agent.authorization.approve and agent.resume cannot launch non-ollama model children
rows.note: Model children are admitted through agenticProviderCheck -> agenticScopeViolation, which allows provider.execute only when provider==='ollama', access==='read' and filesystem===false (authorization.server.ts ~233). Every other child is asked for and then refused. launch() re-runs admitAgenticProvider on the post-reroute task (~1111-1113), so a reroute cannot escape this either. The write-session envelope built by reauthorizeAgent from e.scope (~2066-2110) is not checked by deviceMissionRefusal, but no launch is reachable from it.

rows.title: providers.execution false or sessions undefined cannot launch a provider session
rows.note: scopeFor sets execution true iff a model step exists (authorization.server.ts ~48), and sessions.steps is built from model steps only (~77-81), so the two cannot disagree in a derived scope. taskViolation returns 'provider execution was not approved' when execution is false (~270). approve() refuses a model-step plan without matching sessions (manager ~745-752). providerScopeViolation returns 'authority missing' when sessions is undefined (~255-257) before taskViolation's non-null sessions access. A tool-free model step with no sessions cannot launch.

rows.title: F-01 refuses device approval of every write-session Mission plan, with no bypass found
rows.note: approve() runs deviceMissionRefusal for device actors (~719-721) before any launch. The F-01 check reads requestedScope.providers.sessions.steps, the same object the envelope is built from (envelopeFrom uses requestedScope). The plannedAuthority equality check ties sessions to the current steps (~740-752). Client keys are ignored, and the plan is a Host-computed reference (planReference must equal agenticPlanReference, F-03). Replan requires the workstation. Write children route only to filesystem-capable providers, which are not tool-free.

rows.title: Device submit, feedback, ack and stop do not launch provider sessions
rows.note: submit() never calls launch; the only callers of the private launch() are approve() (~965) and approveDelegated() (~998). The only submit callers are the device-capable HTTP submit (http.server.ts ~549, which leaves the task waiting_for_approval) and launchModel (manager ~1275). feedback() (~1829) only records the value on a terminal task. inbox.ack and stop do not launch.

rows.title: Device skill.run and skill steps cannot launch provider sessions
rows.note: skill.run and skill.verify are not in DEVICE_RIGHTS (http.server.ts ~464) and not in the REMOTE set (commands.server.ts). Skill steps are expanded into concrete capability actions (authorization.server.ts ~50-57 and batch planner ~2975-2985), so a skill never creates a model step. Provider sessions come only from model executors in launchModel.
